notes.bambi: Sympathy: said when something bad happens to someone.
notes.nsonyiwa: An apology for something you did.

guidebook.intro: Most feelings in Lusoga are verbs in the perfect: you have “become tired”, so you are tired. That’s why they look like the past forms from Unit 19.

tips.title: Feelings are states
body: **Nkooye** comes from **-koowa** (get tired), **nsangaire** from **-sanyuka** (become happy), **ntide** from **-tya** (fear). The perfect ending says the change has happened and is still true.
Change the person prefix as usual: **okooye** (you are tired), **akooye** (he/she is tired), **tukooye** (we are tired).

tips.title: Two kinds of sorry
body: **Bambi** shows sympathy: someone is sick, tired or had bad luck, and you feel for them. **Nsonyiwa** (forgive me) is an apology for something you did. Saying **Nsonyiwa** when someone falls over would sound like it was your fault.

culture.title: Asking after everyone
body: Conversations often include news of the whole family: **Maama wo ali atya?** (How is your mother?), **Abaana bali batya?** (How are the children?). Taking time to ask shows real care.
